title: What each Jacobian column means physically

items.stem: For a serial arm, column i of the Jacobian maps joint rates to the motion of the end-effector reference point (the endpoint). Which description of column i is correct?

options.text: The partial derivative of the endpoint's roll-pitch-yaw angles with respect to the joint angle θᵢ
The endpoint's velocity when every joint moves at 1 unit per second, written as one column per joint
The endpoint's linear and angular velocity when only joint i moves, at unit rate, and all other joints are held still
The velocity of the origin of frame i, caused by joint i moving at unit rate

items.stem: A planar arm has two rotary joints with parallel vertical axes. Link 1 is 0.4 m long and link 2 is 0.3 m long, and the arm is stretched out straight. The endpoint is the tip of link 2. Only joint 1 turns, at 2 rad/s, and joint 2 is held still. How fast does the endpoint move, in m/s?

The same planar arm (link 1 is 0.4 m, link 2 is 0.3 m, rotary joints with vertical axes z pointing up) is posed with θ₁ = 0° and θ₂ = 90°. Link 1 lies along the base x-axis, and link 2 points along the base +y-axis, so the endpoint is at (0.4, 0.3, 0) m relative to the base. What is the base-frame x-component of the linear part of Jacobian column 1, in m/s per rad/s? Use the sign that follows from the joint axis z pointing up (counterclockwise rotation is positive).
A prismatic (sliding) joint's axis is the unit vector z in the base frame. Which pair gives the linear part and the angular part of that joint's Jacobian column?

options.text: Linear part z × (Oₙ − Oᵢ₋₁), angular part z
Linear part z × (Oₙ − Oᵢ₋₁), angular part 0

items.stem: In the planar arm above (two rotary joints with parallel vertical axes, link 1 is 0.4 m and link 2 is 0.3 m), what is the angular part, the bottom three entries, of Jacobian column 2?

options.text: (0, 0, 0), because the endpoint's orientation does not change with joint 2
(0, 0, 0.3), because it scales with the length of link 2
(0, 0, 0.4), because it scales with the distance from the base to joint 2
(0, 0, 1), because the endpoint spins about the vertical joint axis at the joint's own rate

items.stem: An arm has rotary and prismatic joints. The Jacobian is first written for the wrist as the endpoint, and then rewritten for a tool tip fixed rigidly 0.2 m beyond the wrist. Which entries of the matrix change?

options.text: The linear and angular parts of every column
Only the linear parts of the rotary-joint columns
The linear parts of every column, rotary and prismatic
Only the linear part of the last column
